title: Reduce GPU memory & workspace usage: activation checkpointing, scratch buffers, arena tuning
author: Priya Nair
description: Context: Large models (1B+ params) occasionally OOM on mid-sized GPU nodes when serving long-context requests. Investigation showed peak workspace allocations from temporary scratch buffers and suboptimal arena allocator sizing. This PR reduces GPU memory and peak workspace usage by: 1) enabling optional activation checkpointing for selected attention/feedforward blocks with a lightweight activation rematerialization API; 2) refactoring the scratch buffer lifetimes so per-layer temporary buffers are reused across operators; 3) tuning the GPU arena allocator defaults to a low-fragmentation growth policy and introducing an env-configurable max-resident threshold; 4) reducing peak KV-cache staging allocations by streaming small batches into the device and reusing pinned host buffers. Motivation: reduce OOM incidents, lower required instance sizes for Dedicated customers, and improve 95th-percentile latency under mixed workloads. Changes are backward compatible and gated behind runtime flags so we can rollout gradually. See linked Linear tasks ENG-4821 and ENG-4830 for benchmarks and rollout plan.

release_notes: Reduced GPU peak memory usage across tested models by 15-30% via optional activation checkpointing, scratch buffer reuse, and arena allocator tuning. Added REDWOOD_GPU_ARENA_MAX_RESIDENT env var and runtime flags to control activation checkpointing and KV-cache streaming. Introduced gpu_arena_fragmentation and gpu_arena_peak_resident metrics. Backward compatible; rollout gated by runtime flags for Dedicated/private deployments.
testing_notes: Benchmarks in tests/perf/bench_gpu_memory_reduction.py show avg peak memory reductions of 18-28% on A100-40GB for 8k context workloads. Added unit tests for scratch pool and activation checkpoint manager. Canary plan: enable flags for 5% of traffic for two weeks, monitor OOMs and p95 latency.
upgrade_instructions: Ops: set REDWOOD_GPU_ARENA_MAX_RESIDENT to a conservative value (e.g., 0.8) for initial rollout. Enable activation checkpointing via runtime config 'enable_activation_checkpointing' per-model. Monitor new metrics gpu_arena_fragmentation and gpu_arena_peak_resident before scaling down instance sizes.
notes: This PR was driven by customer support case SUP-712 and internal infra cost goals. No change to public API surface. Follow-up work: extend checkpointing to decoder-only backbones (ENG-4892).
